# jamfplatform_account_sso_connection (Data Source)

Look up one SSO connection in your Jamf Account organization, by identifier or by the name Jamf Account holds for it. Exactly one of `id` and `name` is required.

This is also the construct for a connection the `jamfplatform_account_sso_connection` resource refuses to manage: one built with Microsoft's admin-consent flow in the Jamf Account console, which has no client registration of its own and cannot be written back. Reading it here takes no ownership of it.

Two things no read returns, so neither appears here: the client secret, which Jamf Account never gives back, and the tenants each product is enabled for. `enabled_product_names` reports the products alone, which is the only part of that assignment that can be read.

**Required Jamf permissions**

Create the API integration with **Organization management** scope, then grant it the following permissions in Jamf Account — see [Getting started with the Platform API](https://developer.jamf.com/platform-api/reference/getting-started-with-platform-api). `Category` and `Permission` name the section and row of the permission picker; `Actions` are the boxes to tick within that row.

| Category | Permission | Actions | API capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organization management scope | SSO connections | Read | `sso-connections` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look a connection up by the identifier Jamf Account assigned it.
data "jamfplatform_account_sso_connection" "by_id" {
  id = "con_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
}

# Or by the name Jamf Account holds for it, which may be a uniquified form of
# the name it was created with. jamfplatform_account_sso_connections reports the
# stored names. Jamf Account does not require them to be unique, so this reports
# an error rather than choosing when more than one matches.
data "jamfplatform_account_sso_connection" "corp" {
  name = "CorpOIDC"
}

output "domains_signed_in_by_this_connection" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_account_sso_connection.corp.domains
}

# The products this connection is enabled for. Only the product names are
# reported; the tenants within each product are not.
output "products" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_account_sso_connection.corp.enabled_product_names
}

# Connections built with Microsoft's admin-consent flow in the Jamf Account
# console have no client registration of their own and cannot be written back, so
# the jamfplatform_account_sso_connection resource refuses to manage one. Reading
# it here takes no ownership of it, and this is how to tell one apart.
output "console_managed" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_account_sso_connection.corp.consent_flow
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Identifier of the connection to look up. Set this or `name`, not both.
- `name` (String) Name Jamf Account holds for the connection, matched exactly. Set this or `id`, not both. Jamf Account may store a uniquified form of the name a connection was created with, so the name to match is the one the console lists rather than the one that was asked for. Use `jamfplatform_account_sso_connections` to see them.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `attribute_map` (String) How claims from the provider are mapped onto Jamf Account user details, as a JSON object string.
- `auth_method` (String) How Jamf Account proves itself to the provider when it redeems an authorization code.
- `client_id` (String) Identifier of the application registered with the provider. Empty for a connection using Microsoft admin consent, which has no client of its own.
- `connection_type` (String) The identity provider family: one of `entra`, `generic_oidc`, `google_workspace`, `okta`.
- `consent_flow` (Boolean) Whether the connection authenticates through Microsoft's admin-consent flow rather than through a registered client. Such a connection cannot be managed as a `jamfplatform_account_sso_connection` resource, so this is how to read one.
- `custom_username_claim_name` (String) The claim a username is read from, where it is not the standard one.
- `domains` (Set of String) The domain names this connection signs people in for.
- `easy_config` (Boolean) Whether the connection was built by Jamf Account's guided setup rather than configured directly.
- `enabled_product_names` (Set of String) The Jamf products Jamf Account reports this connection as enabled for. The tenants of each product are never returned, so this is the whole of what can be read about the assignment.
- `entra` (Attributes) Settings of a Microsoft Entra connection. Empty for every other family. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entra))
- `generic_oidc` (Attributes) Settings of a generic OpenID Connect connection. Empty for every other family. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--generic_oidc))
- `google_workspace` (Attributes) Settings of a Google Workspace connection. Empty for every other family. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--google_workspace))
- `group_name_filter` (Attributes) Which of the provider's groups are passed through to Jamf Account. Empty when the connection carries no filter at all, which is different from a filter with no groups in it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--group_name_filter))
- `hosting_region` (String) The region the connection's provider details are held in and its sign-in traffic is routed through.
- `inactivity_timeout_minutes` (Number) How long a session survives without activity. Empty where the Jamf Account default applies.
- `okta` (Attributes) Settings of an Okta connection. Empty for every other family. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--okta))
- `omit_login_hint` (Boolean) Whether the address someone typed at Jamf Account is withheld from the provider, so they type it again there.
- `pkce` (String) The Proof Key for Code Exchange method used with the provider.
- `scopes` (String) The OAuth scopes Jamf Account asks the provider for, separated by spaces. Empty for a family that takes none.
- `send_nonce` (Boolean) Whether a nonce is sent on the authentication request.
- `session_duration_minutes` (Number) How long a session lasts before the person signs in again, however active they are. Empty where the Jamf Account default applies.
- `sync_attributes_at_login` (Boolean) Whether a person's profile details are refreshed from the provider every time they sign in.
- `ticket_url` (String) Address of the Google Workspace administrator consent request for this connection, where one is outstanding.
- `username_domain` (String) Domain appended to a bare username from the provider to form the person's email address.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--entra"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entra`

Read-Only:

- `basic_profile` (Boolean) Whether a person's basic profile is read from Entra. Always on.
- `domain` (String) Primary domain of the Entra tenant.
- `enable_users_api` (Boolean) Whether Microsoft Graph is queried for details the token does not carry.
- `extended_profile` (Boolean) Whether a person's extended profile details are read from Entra.
- `get_user_groups` (Boolean) Whether a person's Entra group memberships are passed through to Jamf Account.
- `groups_scope` (String) The Microsoft Graph permission groups are read with.
- `identity_api` (String) The Microsoft identity platform version the connection uses.
- `include_nested_groups` (Boolean) Whether groups inherited through nested membership are included.
- `max_groups` (Number) The most groups read for one person.
- `set_emails_verified` (Boolean) Whether addresses from Entra are treated as already confirmed.
- `tenant_domain` (String) Domain identifying the Entra tenant authenticated against.
- `use_common_endpoint` (Boolean) Whether Microsoft's multi-tenant sign-in address is used instead of the tenant's own.
- `use_wsfed` (Boolean) Whether WS-Federation is used instead of OpenID Connect.


<a id="nestedatt--generic_oidc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `generic_oidc`

Read-Only:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) Address people are redirected to in order to sign in.
- `issuer_url` (String) The provider's issuer, as it appears in the tokens it signs.
- `jwks_uri` (String) Address the provider publishes its signing keys at.
- `token_endpoint` (String) Address an authorization code is exchanged at.
- `user_info_endpoint` (String) Address profile details are read from, where the identity token does not carry everything Jamf Account needs.


<a id="nestedatt--google_workspace"></a>
### Nested Schema for `google_workspace`

Read-Only:

- `domain` (String) Primary domain of the Google Workspace account.
- `enable_users_api` (Boolean) Whether the Google Directory is queried for details the token does not carry.
- `extended_groups` (Boolean) Whether groups are read through the Google Directory rather than from the token.
- `get_user_groups` (Boolean) Whether a person's Google Workspace group memberships are passed through to Jamf Account.


<a id="nestedatt--group_name_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `group_name_filter`

Read-Only:

- `groups` (Set of String) The group names filtered on. Empty means no filtering.
- `operator` (String) How the group names are joined: `or` passes a group matching any entry, `and` requires every entry.


<a id="nestedatt--okta"></a>
### Nested Schema for `okta`

Read-Only:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) Address people are redirected to in order to sign in.
- `domain` (String) The Okta org domain.
- `issuer_url` (String) Issuer of the Okta authorization host, worked out from the domain.
- `jwks_uri` (String) Address Okta publishes its signing keys at.
- `token_endpoint` (String) Address an authorization code is exchanged at.
